source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 36 MW of IT load, the fourth largest disclosed figure in Texas, where only 19 of 133 mapped facilities publish capacity at all.

The state's published total of 475 MW is a sum of what operators chose to disclose, so this campus's 7.6% share and its fourth-place rank measure disclosure rather than deployment. A state with 133 mapped facilities and 19 published figures is mostly unmeasured. Any conclusion about Texas data center capacity drawn from these numbers is a conclusion about those 19 sites.

The certifications held here, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, suit finance, healthcare and federal tenants. That is a different workload from the dense AI training clusters driving recent demand. At an assumed 40 kW per rack, 36 MW is roughly 900 racks, and 296,000 square feet of technical space at that density suggests the published figure covers the current footprint rather than a future buildout.

What is absent is the part that matters most for AI scaling. No power supply arrangement, grid interconnection or expansion plan is published for this site. The suitability score of 68 is computed from published IT capacity and operator type alone, with announced expansion listed as missing. Nothing here establishes whether the campus can obtain more power, which is the constraint that decides whether it grows.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
